memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had explored the land, tore their clothes and said to the entire Israelite assembly, "The land we passed through and explored is exceedingly good. If the Lord is pleased with us, he will lead us into that land, a land flowing with milk and honey, and will give it to us. Only do not rebel against the Lord. And do not be afraid of the people of the land, because we will devour them. Their protection is gone, but the Lord is with us. Do not be afraid of them." — Num 14:6-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two men stand against an entire nation. Joshua and Caleb tear their clothes in grief and plead with the crowd, risking their own lives to speak the truth. When everyone else has surrendered to fear, these two refuse to be silent. Faith sometimes means standing almost alone.

Listen to the heart of their appeal. First, the land is good — God's promise is trustworthy. Second, "if the Lord is pleased with us, he will lead us." Everything hinges not on Israel's strength but on God's presence and favour. And then the key line: "The Lord is with us. Do not be afraid." The giants had lost their protection; the Israelites had gained the Almighty.

This is the great truth that fear always forgets: the Lord is with us. The ten spies had done all their math and left God out. Joshua and Caleb put Him back into the equation, and suddenly the giants shrink. The difference between courage and cowardice is often simply whether we remember who is with us.

For those who belong to Christ, this promise is even surer. Jesus said, "I am with you always." The Spirit of God lives within us. Whatever giants you face, you do not face them alone. "Do not be afraid" is not a call to pretend the danger away, but a call to remember the greater reality: the Lord is with you. Let that steady you when the crowd around you trembles.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you willing to stand for truth even when almost everyone disagrees?
2. How does remembering "the Lord is with us" change the size of your giants?
3. What fear do you need to answer today with "the Lord is with me"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me the courage of Joshua and Caleb to stand for truth against the crowd. Help me never to leave You out of my calculations. Thank You that in Christ You are with me always, so I need not be afraid. Amen.
